findings.summary: colpali-v1.3 retrieves correctly on a real ViDoRe slice through the unchanged upstream CLI: nDCG@5 0.89682 and recall@3 1.0 on 12 TabFQuAD rows, against 0.19678 and 0.25 for the built-in random-embedding control on the same rows. The control's embeddings come from torch.randn under the CLI's fixed seed 42, so its metrics are identical in every run.

vidore/colqwen2.5-v0.2 was not evaluated. It is not selectable through the vidore-benchmark 5.0.0 CLI: no retriever is registered for ColQwen2.5 (the colqwen2 retriever loads ColQwen2/ColQwen2Processor, while colqwen2.5-v0.2's base declares architectures ColQwen2_5, model_type qwen2_5_vl). The documented 5.0.0 Python API (VisionRetriever(model, processor) in ViDoReEvaluatorQA, for retrievers outside the CLI list; the processor needs process_images, process_queries and score) accepts colpali-engine 0.3.13's ColQwen2_5 and ColQwen2_5_Processor, but it was not tried. The colqwen2-v1.0 attempts failed while loading the processor, not on the architecture: since 2026-08-17 both Hub repositories carry additional_chat_templates/sentence_transformers.jinja, and transformers 4.53.1 and 4.57.6 (the ends of colpali-engine 0.3.13's range) request it as .jinja.jinja, get None and raise the TypeError in open(). transformers 5.0.0 strips the suffix, but colpali-engine 0.3.13 requires transformers <4.58.0. The probe showed the same TypeError for ColQwen2_5_Processor at the pinned colqwen2.5-v0.2 revision dcbe8d9c, and that both processors load at the last revision without the template (83a0134c, 6f6fcdfd).

The PyPI-latest colpali-engine (0.3.18) cannot be installed with vidore-benchmark 5.0.0 (transformers>=5.3.0 against sentence-transformers<4, which needs transformers<5); it does install with mteb 2.21.8 and sentence-transformers 6.1.0, the path vidore-benchmark's main README now points to, which this trial did not evaluate.

On CPU a 3B ColPali model is slow: 149 s per batch of 4 page images in the reproduction (load average 22-28); 206-266 s (slice) and 162-243 s (full split) per batch in the first pass under heavier contention, taken from the logs' elapsed stamps rather than tqdm's smoothed s/it column. The 12-row slice took 529 s wall and 9315.11 CPU-seconds (8905.32 user plus 409.79 system) with a peak RSS of 41,712,648 KiB = 42.7 GB (39.8 GiB) by /usr/bin/time -v. The first pass reported a peak RSS of about 8 GB, which the reproduction does not support.

Without CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' the CLI uses the GPU whenever one is visible (device 'auto'). The first pass's receipt runs relied on that default while claiming a CPU run; their 105-119 s durations are GPU-indicated, not CPU.

The first pass's run stopped after 6 of 70 image batches; how it ended is not retained. The CLI embeds the image of every query row (280 images in 70 batches of 4), so at the observed 149-243 s per batch the full split needs about 2.9 to 4.7 hours of image embedding plus about 5 minutes of queries on this CPU. The trial ran on CPU by intent.
